title: Blackberry and apple compote with crunchy oats

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Apples, blackberries, honey, oats, hazelnuts, Greek yoghurt, cinnamon and lemon are all plain kitchen staples.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at any mainstream UK supermarket, and blackberries are cheap in August.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a small pan and a frying pan, and simmering fruit and toasting oats are beginner techniques.

works.reason: 300g blackberries, 2 apples, 500g yoghurt and 80g oats with nuts make a sensible breakfast for four, and the simmer times suit diced apple and soft berries.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes is believable for peeling and dicing two apples, chopping hazelnuts and stirring the toasting oats, and 8 minutes matches the 5 plus 3 minute simmer.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, nothing unlisted appears apart from water, and lemon is on the August fresh list.

seasonal_feel.reason: Early August is blackberry season and the berries are the centre of the compote, not a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear and homely, in plain British English.

hearty_healthy.reason: Fruit, yoghurt, oats and nuts with only 2 tbsp honey make a filling, wholesome breakfast a family would happily eat again.
